references.text: Jesus quotes directly from Deuteronomy 6:16: "You shall not put the Lord your God to the test." This is the source text from the Old Testament that Jesus uses to reject the devil's temptation.
The background for the command in Deuteronomy 6:16 is the incident at Massah, where the Israelites put the Lord to the test by demanding water and doubting whether God was among them.
The parallel passage in Matthew's account of the temptation, where Jesus answers the devil with the same quote from Deuteronomy 6:16: "You shall not put the Lord your God to the test."

The broader context in Deuteronomy 6 about fearing the Lord, serving Him alone, and not following other gods – which forms the framework for the prohibition against putting God to the test in verse 16.
The full account of Jesus' temptation in the wilderness in Luke, where Jesus three times rejects the devil by quoting from Scripture – all the quotes are taken from Deuteronomy.
Paul warns against putting Christ to the test, as some of the Israelites did in the desert – a direct connection to the theme of not tempting the Lord.
The psalmist warns against hardening the heart as the fathers did at Massah and Meribah, where they put God to the test – the same incident that lies behind Jesus' quote.
Moses explains that God humbled the people and let them hunger in the desert to test them – a background that contrasts with the devil's attempt to get Jesus to put God to the test.
